The Yolo County Superior Court is a city courthouse in Yolo County, California. It is located within the ninth circuit of the United State Court of Appeals. It was constructed in 1864 and rebuilt into a new courthouse with 14 courtrooms in 2015. The court has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims and probation matters, as well as juvenile, civil, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. They provide online services like files, online payment, forms, remote traffic appearances, probate notes, court calendars and many more, so it is optional to go to court for these services. It also provides self-help appointments, remote court appearances and live courthouse view. Every person must follow local rules in this court. Career opportunities are also available. How to search for case information?

Yolo County Superior Court Case Search can be done online using the intelligent search facility offered by this court to find case records. The search can be done in the following ways:

  • Searching by record or case number
  • Searching by First and Last name.

After entering the data, the information will display. If the information does not come, then the case records will be confidential and cannot be displayed online. You have to go to the court and give a request for these types of documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information to you or not.

How can a hearing search be done?

Yolo County Superior Court case hearing search can be online using search types and hearing dates. The search types can be done in the following ways:

  • Search by Case Number
  • Search by Party Name
  • Search by Business Name
  • Search by Attorney Name
  • Examination by Attorney Bar Number
  • Search by Judicial Officer
  • Search by Courtroom

After entering data from these following ways, Date from and To is mandatory, the hearing search for the case will display.

How can I make a payment?

Yolo County Superior Court fines and traffic tickets payments can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the payment center. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.5% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

Online traffic tickets or other fines payments can be made using the Superior Court Online Portal https://www.ncourt.com/ncourtlanding/cayolocountylanding.aspx. Enter the Ticket/Citation, case, and driving license number. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's collection division at 1000 Main St, Woodland, CA 95695. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Telephone

Payment can also be made by calling directly at 530-406-6924. Tell them your case number and credit card number. A convenience fee will be applied in this case.

How can live streaming for the courtroom be viewed?

Yolo County Superior Court live stream channel option is available by this court. These channels aim to provide the court hearing public access using online streaming. The court has the right to allow which content will be shared with the audience during the live stream. You can view the courtroom live stream by clicking on the department number you want to watch the streaming.

How can a person take remote hearings for cases?

Yolo County Superior Court remote appearance facility was introduced during the coronavirus, done by zoom application. If your case is eligible for remote appearance, fill out the form and submit it online. You can get an email in which the schedule and the meeting link are given to you. Join the link ten minutes before the actual schedule. If you do not have internet access, remote hearing can be done by calling 669-900-9128, 669-219-2599, or 213-338-8477.

How can I file my case using an e-file?

Yolo County Superior Court e-file can be done when you want to file for cases online-file can be done by three steps:

  • Please answer all the questions online; it can help in the preparation of your case
  • Legal Documents will create automatically after the answers
  • The online case will be filed online

How can I file for small claim cases?

Yolo County Superior Court's small claim division handles all the small claims matters in which claims are up to $10,000.This court will handle all the disputes related to a person or a property very quickly and in inexpensive ways. Fill out the form for small claims online or by visiting the court and fill in all the personal information of the defendant and plaintiff; tell the reason for claiming and the amount you are suing. The defendant must be from this county only; otherwise, the case will not be taken.

How much are the fees for appealing?

Yolo County Superior Court appealing fees depend upon the type of cases you request to appeal. $225 to $370 is the fee for limited civil case appeals, $775 for unlimited civil court case appeals, and $559 for the petition fees of Writ within the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction.

This court hears which types of juvenile cases?

Yolo County Superior Court juvenile division handles some cases involving juvenile involvement. Two types of case proceedings are done in this court that are:

  • The juvenile dependency in which a neglected or abused child case is involved
  • Juvenile dependency is when a committed delinquent act by the child is involved.

Contact the division by visiting or calling them during working hours if you need any information.

The civil division handles which types of cases?

Yolo County Superior Court civil division handles all the matters and disputes in which one party sues another party, harassment or fights cases that the party does not control. This division also protects the rights of citizens. You can also request an interpreter if you are involved in a civil case. The civil case hearing is also done remotely using the zoom application.

The family division handles which types of cases?

Yolo County Superior Court family division handles family matters that include:

  • Divorce, legal separation
  • Child Custody and Visitation
  • Rights of Parents
  • Domestic Violence
  • Spouse and Child support

This court provides child custody recommendation counseling and a self-help center facility. Contact this division by visiting or calling them during working hours if you need any information.

How can I search for my criminal case information?

Yolo County Superior Court criminal case search information can be found online using https://www.yolo.courts.ca.gov/service-currently-unavailable, or you can call 530-406-6705 to get assistance from the deputy clerk about the case information. If you are involved in any criminal cases, you can appear in court by bringing some documents that include: a citation copy, letter of appearance, Bond or cash receipt, and fine or fees related to the case.
